about: ScanRuler for FreeCAD's Mesh Tools added headless (Densify, Boolean, Trim to scan, Shell, Wrap), in Agent Link's tool-data format, to merge into data/tools.json. Handlers: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py; ported from ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen).

mesh_densify.description: Cut the triangles until no edge is longer than maxEdge, the surface unchanged: every new vertex is an edge's middle, on the facet it was cut from, and the mesh stays as closed as it was. For an STL exported from CAD, whose vertices lie only on its edges and rims: a segmentation, a seeded fit or a section fit finds points inside its faces only after it. A scan needs none. maxEdge defaults to a hundredth of the part on the 1-2-5 steps. Edits the copy. Returns the edit (maxEdge, the vertices added, the triangles now) and the mesh after it.

maxEdge.description: No edge longer than this, mm.

mesh_densify.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_boolean.description: Make the mesh and solids one: subtract them from it, add them to it, or intersect (keep what both hold). The solids: the cylinders, cones and spheres measured (elements, by id or name, at their assumed diameter), or solid bodies in the FreeCAD document (by Name or Label). Several go as one, their union. The mesh must be closed (mesh_inspect; mesh_fill_holes first). For a bore the scanner could not see to the bottom of: fit a cylinder to its wall, make it longer than the bore and out through the surface, and subtract it. FreeCAD's Mesh booleans do the cut (unavailable outside FreeCAD). Edits the copy. Returns the edit (the volume change) and the mesh after it.

solids.description: The solids, by element id or name, or document object Name or Label.

mesh_boolean.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_shell.description: A closed part is hollowed: its outside stays as scanned and an inner wall thickness in from it seals a cavity (where the part is thinner than twice the wall it stays solid). An open surface — one side of a part, a sheet — is thickened into a solid: a second skin thickness from it, side in (the scanned surface stays the outside), out or both, and a wall round every rim. A part closed but for holes smaller than the Fill holes size is refused: fill them (mesh_fill_holes) to hollow it, or pass mode: "thicken" to thicken it as it is. thickness defaults to a 125th of the part's diagonal. Edits the copy. Returns the edit and the mesh after it.

thickness.description: The wall a hollow leaves, or the thickness a surface is given, mm.

side.description: For a surface: which way the wall grows from it — in to start.

mode.description: What to do; absent, what the mesh calls for.

mesh_shell.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_wrap.description: One closed skin round the mesh worked on — the edited copy, or the scan — for a mesh that is a mess inside: an assembly exported as one file, channels and bosses inside a casting, overlapping or flipped shells, a scan with cracks. Any triangles do: only the distance to them is used. A ball of diameter gap is rolled round the mesh from outside; the wrap lies on the part where the ball touched it and bridges every opening narrower than gap — a groove narrower than it is closed over too, so keep it small. Everything inside is dropped. grow (0 to start, at most gap) stands the wrap off the part all round: an open sheet wraps to nothing at 0, and to a slab 2 × grow thick. edges: sharp (to start) rebuilds the part's sharp edges and corners where the wrap lies on the part; smooth leaves them rounded by the grid, a sixth of the gap. Made beside the mesh — a preview: mesh_apply_wrap makes it the edited copy, or preview: false applies it at once. Returns the wrap: shells, triangles, dropped (input triangles inside it), bridgedArea (mm²), volumeBefore (null when the mesh is open) and volume (mm³), cell (the grid, mm; coarsened, and fullGap, when the part's size made it coarser than a sixth of the gap), sharpEdges and sharpCorners.

gap.description: Openings narrower than this are bridged, mm.

grow.description: How far the wrap stands off the part, mm: 0 to start, at most gap.

tolerance.description: How far the wrap's reduction may stray from it, mm (kept for when a reducer is ported).

preview.description: false applies the wrap at once as the edited copy; true (to start) leaves it a preview for mesh_apply_wrap.

mesh_wrap.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_apply_wrap.description: Make the wrap on hand the edited copy: the tools work on it from here, and mesh_use_edited takes it into use. None of the mesh's vertices is kept. One undo step, which puts the mesh it was made of back. Returns the edit and the mesh.
mesh_apply_wrap.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_trim.description: Mend a broken part: cut a body — the missing piece modelled to the part's nominal shape and a few millimetres too long at the break — with the scanned fracture, to print and glue in. The body: a solid body in the FreeCAD document (Name or Label), or a measured cylinder, cone or sphere. The break is where the scan lies deeper in the body than depth (0.3 mm to start); region names it instead. offset sets the mating face back from the break (0 cuts on it, a tenth or two leaves room for glue); flip keeps the other side. FreeCAD's Mesh booleans do the cut (unavailable outside FreeCAD). The piece is made beside the scan, not an edit of it. Returns the piece: its volume, mating face, and how far that face is from the part.

offset.description: How far the mating face sits back from the break, mm.

depth.description: How much deeper in the body than its surface the scan must lie to be break, mm.

flip.description: Keep what is on the other side of the break.

region.description: The surface: { box: { min, max } }, { sphere: { center, radius } } or { vertices: [...] } (as mesh_smooth takes), optionally with facing.

mesh_trim.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py
